narrative.overview:
Zoomies is a watch room, not a dashboard. The operator leaves it open on a second monitor through a working day, so the surface is quiet at rest, unmistakable when something needs a person, and dense enough that a useful number of runners fit without scrolling. The visual language is instrument grade: Inter at operational sizes, a 4px grid, precise borders and restrained cool shadows. The dog-park identity sits underneath that discipline as a warm signature, in the mark, the artwork, the empty states and the vocabulary, never as chrome on an operational row.

The default world is Mission Control: navy surfaces in dark mode, cool paper in light mode, Runner Blue for interaction and Fast Cyan spent on the one thing that is actually moving. Dark is the opening theme. A page opens with a black band that states the answer before the evidence, then panels, grids and tiles that carry the detail. Status is always carried by colour and shape together, because an operator glancing from across the room must not need hue alone.

Refinement preserves this world. A redesign may replace the composition, but keeps the product truth: every resource is visible without a refresh, every status means one thing, and every number is tabular so columns agree.
keyCharacteristics: Calm at rest, loud only where the fleet is wrong.
Navy Mission Control surfaces, dark by default, with a fixed black page band.
Dense Inter type on a strict 4px rhythm, never smaller than a person can read.
Colour plus shape for every state; cyan exclusively means work in progress.
Tonal layering and hairlines first, shadows only for overlays and state.
Dog-park warmth in art and words, never in the operational grammar.

rules.name: The Cyan Is Busy Rule
rules.body: Fast Cyan and its Mission Control value may only mean "work is executing now". No note, badge, chart series or decorative flourish may borrow it.

rules.name: The Six Mean Six Things Rule
rules.body: Idle, busy, pending, draining, danger and neutral are a fixed vocabulary. They are never reused for categories, brands or decoration, and each is also drawn as a distinct shape.

rules.name: The Information Is Not A Status Rule
rules.body: A note, hint or informational box uses Command Blue and its subtle ground. It never wears one of the six status hues.

rules.name: The Dense-But-Readable Rule
rules.body: Mission Control body text is 14px; Classic is 13px. Nothing an operator must read goes below 12px. Small caps are not a substitute for hierarchy.

rules.name: The Absent Value Rule
rules.body: A missing value is two hyphens, written from the NO_VALUE constant, never an em dash or an en dash. A formatter that has no value returns the same mark, so a tile and the table beneath it agree.

rules.name: The Error Replaces The Hint Rule
rules.body: A field shows one message row. A validation error takes the hint's place rather than adding a line, so nothing below it moves under a pointer that is already on its way to the submit button.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A card, panel or tile carries no shadow until state asks for one. Hover changes surface or border, not height.

rules.name: The One Veil Rule
rules.body: Every modal uses the same scrim and blur from the token file. A second dimming recipe is a bug.

rules.name: The Border Weight Is Meaning Rule
rules.body: If two edges differ in thickness, they differ in meaning. Do not add a third weight for looks.

rules.name: The Square-Shouldered Rule
rules.body: Pills are for dots and badges, not buttons, cards or navigation. A card is a rounded rectangle, not a lozenge.

dos: Do take every colour, radius, space and duration from the token file; a value used twice belongs there.
Do pair every status colour with its shape, and keep Fast Cyan for running work alone.
Do keep the page band black in both themes, and keep its accent and lede legible on that fixed ground.
Do use tabular numerals in every table and figure column.
Do keep a dense 32px control rhythm on desktop and step to touch sizes only under a coarse pointer or the phone breakpoint.
Do let a grid fill its frame, sharing spare width among columns the operator has not sized.
Do use the dog artwork in the brand moments, empty states and first run, where it carries warmth without competing with the fleet.
donts: Don't introduce glows, gradient text, glassmorphism, decorative sparkles, oversized rounded cards or charts that exist to fill space.
Don't reuse a status hue for a category, a chart series or a note.
Don't write a raw colour or a one-off radius in a component.
Don't make a mascot part of an operational row, a table cell or a control.
Don't animate layout or reflow a table while an operator is reading it; animate colour, the dot and the panel, at 120ms to 320ms.
Don't remove the focus ring or replace it with a colour change.
Don't write an em dash or an en dash as the absent value; use the NO_VALUE mark.
